clue.text: More surprised than one can say?

definitions.text: More surprised than one can say?

parts.words: More surprised than one can say?
parts.note: someone so astonished that words fail them is literally left without speech, which is the condition named

explanation.surface: A question about being so amazed you cannot find the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rendered speechless by shock is exactly the idiom's meaning, so surprise beyond words fits it.

clue.text: Journalist following game was made to seem small

indicators.note: the journalist's letters come after, or follow, the game's letters

parts.note: squash is a racket game played in a walled court
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter tagging along after a match ends up belittled.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash someone is to humiliate or crush them, making them feel insignificant.

clue.text: Not a common find

parts.note: something seldom come across is an unusual discovery, read straight as the definition

explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce or unusual, seldom met with, is the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Actors performing share lead

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of Actors are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: Players on stage split the starring role between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer billed equally with another shares the principal role, the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Used when main meal of the day is prepared

definitions.text: Used when main meal of the day is prepared

parts.words: Used when main meal of the day is prepared
parts.note: the matching plates and dishes are brought out when the evening table is laid; the clue also hints at dinner plus set, meaning prepared

explanation.surface: Something brought into service when the evening meal is ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching collection of crockery is laid out for the principal meal, which is what this set is for.

clue.text: Herb took Charlie into Iowa church

parts.note: basil is a common culinary herb

indicators.note: the letter for Charlie is placed into the state's abbreviation

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa
Charlie is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter C

explanation.surface: A man named Herb drove Charlie to a church in Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often one granted special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Mock drill after getting German agreement

indicators.note: the drill's letters come after the German yes has been obtained

parts.note: ja is German for yes
PE, physical education, is exercise or drill

explanation.surface: A soldier ridicules the parade-ground routine once the German says yes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to jape is to jest at or make fun of, the same as to ridicule.

clue.text: Joseph, good man with heather, elbowing

parts.note: Jo is a short form of Joseph
ST, saint, is the crossword's good man
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Joseph and a virtuous friend push their way through the moorland heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing and shoving with the elbows in a crowd is the same as jostling.

clue.text: Fighting in the shops?

parts.note: not a brawl among shoppers but retailers competing by cutting what they charge

explanation.definitionFit: Competing retailers repeatedly undercutting each other's charges is a commercial battle, hence the conflict metaphor.

clue.text: Rebellion at university becoming hostile

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
rising, as in rising against rulers, is turning hostile in revolt

explanation.surface: Students at college turn aggressive and revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular revolt or insurrection against authority is a rebellion.

clue.text: Bird one's put in film

indicators.note: the letters for one's are put inside the word for a film

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer, as on custard
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An actor's pet bird gets cast in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Set daughter had placed in a certain position

parts.note: to situate something is to set or place it

explanation.surface: A girl's parent has fixed her in a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something located or sited at a particular spot is set in that position.

clue.text: Girl and boy shortly sang merrily

parts.note: Lil is a short form of the girl's name Lillian
Ted is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A young couple briefly sang a cheerful song together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' tells you both names are pet forms, Lil and Ted, rather than signalling any letter removal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lilt is to sing or speak with a light, cheerful rhythmic swing.

clue.text: Punter's pecuniary gains from gamble

indicators.note: gains here means takes in or contains, so the letters sit inside the punter's words

explanation.surface: A bettor's financial winnings come from taking a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation is a risky venture, so buying on spec is a gamble.

clue.text: Scope in joint apartment?

parts.note: the elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm
a room is a chamber or apartment of a house

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is space inside a shared flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Space to move freely, or freedom of action, is what scope means.

clue.text: Recruit found floating structure in river

indicators.note: the raft's letters are placed in the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
a raft is a flat floating platform

explanation.surface: A new soldier is discovered on a raft drifting down the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conscripted into the armed forces is a new recruit.

clue.text: Pasta, one gram included in revised ration

indicators.note: one and gram go inside the reworked letters
revised means the letters of ration are reworked into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A recipe note: pasta, measured to a single gram within a changed allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a recipe allowance; 'revised' scrambles the six letters and 'included in' sets the Roman one and the gram abbreviation inside them, just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ribbed tube-shaped Italian pasta.

clue.text: Plant's beastly cover that's handy?

parts.note: beastly is read as belonging to a beast, here the fox
a glove covers the hand

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a plant is an animal's useful covering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Plant stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a tall flowering plant, the source of digitalis.

clue.text: Alienate sergeant in mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of sergeant are thrown into disorder; it also plays on the army mess

explanation.surface: Upsetting the sergeant in the military dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them unfriendly or distant, to alienate them.

clue.text: Dawdler did not finish exchanging glad rags

indicators.note: exchanging means the letters swap places among themselves
the last word is not completed, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A slowcoach did not complete changing out of party clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not finish' cuts RAGS to RAG; 'exchanging' rearranges GLADRAG into the answer. Glad rags are one's best party clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is someone who falls behind or is slow, a dawdler.

clue.text: Does Frenchman included take 24 hours to get this book?

indicators.note: the Frenchman's letter is included inside the word Does

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
a day lasts 24 hours

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Frenchman needs a whole day to obtain a particular volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Domesday Book is the great survey of England compiled for William the Conqueror in 1086.

clue.text: Attempt to put the knife in?

definitions.meaning: an attempt is a try, as in having a go
to wound with a pointed blade

explanation.surface: A try at stabbing someone with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A go or try at something is one sense; thrusting a blade into someone is the other.

clue.text: Absolutely correct, but it doesn't get the mark off

definitions.text: it doesn't get the mark off
definitions.meaning: a stain that remains is a mark still present, a blemish left on

explanation.surface: Something perfectly accurate, yet unable to clean a stain away.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly right is the idiom; read literally, a blemish that stays put is a spot remaining in place.

clue.text: Silky wool from Penang or astrakhan

indicators.note: from tells you the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Fine fleece imported from Malaysia or a Russian lambskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is the soft fibre from Angora goats or rabbits.

clue.text: Noisy old car?

parts.note: a clapped-out vehicle that backfires; the word also suggests something that goes bang

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a BANGER is also a sausage and a firework, the noisy sense.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names a dilapidated motor this way, and it fits one that bangs and backfires.

clue.text: Couple at enclosure with this French money!

parts.note: a couple is two
a pen is an enclosure for animals
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A pair at the sheep pen exclaim in French about the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TWOPENCE is an old British coin worth two pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Twopence is a small sum of British currency, a coin worth two pennies.

clue.text: 'Care of' written twice on envelope

indicators.note: written twice means the abbreviation appears two times in a row

parts.note: c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of in addresses

explanation.surface: Someone has addressed a letter with 'c/o' repeated twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is a silky case that envelops a pupa, a protective covering.

clue.text: As many as can be put in a packet perhaps

definitions.text: As many as can be put in a packet perhaps

parts.words: As many as can be put in a packet perhaps
parts.note: a packet here is a packet boat, a mail steamer, so the full cargo it carries is meant, not a small parcel

explanation.surface: How much fits inside a small parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A full cargo carried by a vessel such as a packet steamer is its complete shipload.

clue.text: Measurement started in Zambia initially going eastward

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of each of the words started, in and Zambia

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A survey that began in Zambia then headed east.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is a thing's dimensions or extent, what a measurement records.

clue.text: Meteorological?

parts.note: weather is the elements, so anything to do with them could whimsically be described this way

explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean relating to the elements, and wind and rain are the elements in everyday speech.
